body:
In this article, you will learn how to convert SVG to PDF in Python. You will start with a single function call, then control the page size, background, and document properties, and finally convert a whole folder of SVG files in one run.

PDF is the format most people expect when they print, archive, or email a graphic. An [SVG](https://docs.fileformat.com/page-description-language/svg/) file is perfect for the web, but not every document workflow can open it. Converting it to [PDF](https://docs.fileformat.com/pdf/) gives you a fixed-layout file that keeps the vector shapes and text sharp at any zoom level.

## Python SVG to PDF Converter Library

The examples use [Aspose.SVG for Python via .NET](https://products.aspose.com/svg/python-net/), an API for loading, editing, and rendering SVG documents. It renders the SVG itself, so you don't need a browser, Inkscape, or Cairo installed on the machine.

Install the package from PyPI:

```bash
pip install aspose-svg-net
```

You can also download it from the [releases page](https://releases.aspose.com/svg/python-net/).

The examples below use this `sample.svg` file. Save it in your project folder to follow along:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="300" viewBox="0 0 400 300">
  <rect x="20" y="20" width="160" height="100" fill="#4A90E2" stroke="#1F3B63" stroke-width="4"/>
  <circle cx="290" cy="80" r="55" fill="#F5A623" stroke="#8B5A00" stroke-width="4"/>
  <line x1="20" y1="170" x2="380" y2="170" stroke="#333333" stroke-width="3"/>
  <text x="200" y="240" font-family="Arial" font-size="36" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2C3E50">Aspose.SVG</text>
</svg>
```

## Convert SVG to PDF in Python

The shortest route is the `Converter.convert_svg()` method. It takes the source document, a save-options object, and the output path.

Follow these steps to convert an SVG file to PDF:

1. Load the SVG file into an `SVGDocument`.
2. Create a `PdfSaveOptions` object.
3. Call `Converter.convert_svg()` with the document, the options, and the output file name.

The following code example converts `sample.svg` to `sample.pdf`:

```python
import aspose.svg as svg
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import PdfSaveOptions

# Load the SVG document
document = svg.SVGDocument("sample.svg")

# Convert SVG to PDF with default options
Converter.convert_svg(document, PdfSaveOptions(), "sample.pdf")
```

With the default options, the drawing is placed on an **A4 page**. That is useful for print layouts, but if you want the PDF page to match the graphic, set the page sizing as shown in the next section.

## Fit the PDF Page to the SVG and Set a Background

The `PdfSaveOptions` controls how the SVG is laid out in the PDF. The options you will use most often are:

* `page_setup.sizing`: set it to `SizingType.FIT_CONTENT` to make the page the same size as the drawing.
* `page_setup.any_page`: set an exact page size instead, for example 400 × 300 pixels.
* `background_color`: fill transparent areas with a solid color. SVG backgrounds are transparent by default.
* `jpeg_quality`: the JPEG compression quality for raster images embedded in the SVG.

The following code example fits the page to the drawing and adds a white background:

```python
import aspose.svg as svg
import aspose.pydrawing as drawing
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import PdfSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType

document = svg.SVGDocument("sample.svg")

options = PdfSaveOptions()
# Make the PDF page the same size as the SVG drawing
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT
# Fill transparent areas with white
options.background_color = drawing.Color.white

Converter.convert_svg(document, options, "sample-fit.pdf")
```

To use a fixed page size instead, define a `Page` with a `Size` built from `Unit` values. Note that `Unit.from_pixels()` expects a float:

```python
import aspose.svg as svg
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import PdfSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.drawing import Page, Size, Unit

document = svg.SVGDocument("sample.svg")

options = PdfSaveOptions()
# Use a 600 x 400 pixel page
options.page_setup.any_page = Page(Size(Unit.from_pixels(600.0), Unit.from_pixels(400.0)))

Converter.convert_svg(document, options, "sample-600x400.pdf")
```

## Add a Title and Author to the PDF

When the PDF is going into a document library or an archive, set its properties so it shows a useful title in viewers and search results. Use the `document_info` property of `PdfSaveOptions`:

```python
import aspose.svg as svg
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import PdfSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType

document = svg.SVGDocument("sample.svg")

options = PdfSaveOptions()
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT
# Set PDF document properties
options.document_info.title = "Quarterly Sales Chart"
options.document_info.author = "Reporting Team"

Converter.convert_svg(document, options, "sample-with-info.pdf")
```

## Convert an SVG from a URL to PDF

`Converter.convert_svg()` also accepts a file path or a URL as its first argument, so you don't have to create an `SVGDocument` first:

```python
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import PdfSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType

options = PdfSaveOptions()
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT

# Convert an SVG published on the web
Converter.convert_svg("https://www.w3.org/Icons/SVG/svg-logo-v.svg", options, "svg-logo.pdf")
```

## Batch Convert SVG Files to PDF

If you have a folder of icons, charts, or diagrams, loop over the files and reuse the same options object. Each SVG becomes its own PDF:

```python
import os
import glob
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import PdfSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType

input_dir = "svg-files"
output_dir = "pdf-files"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

options = PdfSaveOptions()
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT

for svg_path in glob.glob(os.path.join(input_dir, "*.svg")):
    name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(svg_path))[0]
    pdf_path = os.path.join(output_dir, name + ".pdf")
    Converter.convert_svg(svg_path, options, pdf_path)
    print("Converted:", pdf_path)
```

If you want all the SVG files in **one** PDF instead, see [Merge SVG Files into PDF in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/merge-svg-files-into-pdf-in-python/).

## Get a Free License

Without a license, Aspose.SVG runs in evaluation mode and adds an evaluation notice to the output. Request a [free temporary license](https://purchase.aspose.com/temporary-license/) to test the conversion without these limits.

## Convert SVG to PDF Online

For a one-off file, you can use the free [online SVG to PDF converter](https://products.aspose.app/svg/conversion/svg-to-pdf). Upload the SVG in your browser, choose a page size, and download the PDF. Use the Python API when you need to convert files automatically or inside your own application.

## SVG to PDF: Free Resources

* [Aspose.SVG for Python Documentation](https://docs.aspose.com/svg/python-net/)
* [Aspose.SVG for Python API Reference](https://reference.aspose.com/svg/python-net/)
* [Free Online SVG Apps](https://products.aspose.app/svg/family)
* [Aspose.SVG Blog Posts](https://blog.aspose.com/categories/aspose.svg-product-family/)

## SVG to PDF in Python: FAQs

**Q: Why is my SVG placed on an A4 page in the PDF?**

A: `PdfSaveOptions` uses an A4 page by default. Set `options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT` to make the page match the drawing.

**Q: Does the PDF keep the SVG as vector graphics?**

A: Shapes, paths and text are written as vector content, so they stay sharp when zoomed. Raster images embedded in the SVG remain raster images.

**Q: Can I convert an SVG from a URL to PDF?**

A: Yes. Pass the URL to `SVGDocument` or directly to `Converter.convert_svg()`.

**Q: Can I combine several SVG files into one PDF?**

A: Yes. Use `SvgRenderer` with a `PdfDevice` to render several documents into a single multi-page PDF.

## Conclusion

You can now convert SVG to PDF in Python with a single `Converter.convert_svg()` call, fit the page to the drawing, add a background and document properties, and process a whole folder at once. As a next step, try rendering the same SVG to an image format: the [SVG to JPG](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/convert-svg-to-jpg-in-python/) and [SVG to PNG](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/convert-svg-to-png-in-python/) guides use the same pattern with `ImageSaveOptions`.

If you run into a file that doesn't convert as expected, post it on the [Aspose.SVG free support forum](https://forum.aspose.com/c/svg/42).

## See Also

* [Convert SVG to JPG in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/convert-svg-to-jpg-in-python/)
* [Convert SVG to PNG in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/convert-svg-to-png-in-python/)
* [Merge SVG Files into PDF in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/merge-svg-files-into-pdf-in-python/)
* [Convert SVG Code to PNG in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/convert-svg-code-to-png-in-python/)
* [Change SVG Fill Color in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/change-svg-fill-color-in-python/)
* [Optimize SVG in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/optimize-svg-image-in-python/)

body:
This guide shows you how to convert SVG to PNG in Python when your SVG lives in a file or at a web address. You will convert a single file, convert an SVG straight from a URL, set the PNG's pixel size, and process a whole folder in one loop.

[PNG](https://docs.fileformat.com/image/png/) is the usual target when an [SVG](https://docs.fileformat.com/page-description-language/svg/) has to go somewhere that doesn't display vector graphics: a mobile app, a slide, a document, or an image pipeline. PNG supports transparency, so icons and logos keep their clear background.

If your SVG is generated as markup in a string, see [Convert SVG Code to PNG in Python](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/convert-svg-code-to-png-in-python/), which covers string input and in-memory rendering.

## Python Library to Convert SVG to PNG

The examples use [Aspose.SVG for Python via .NET](https://products.aspose.com/svg/python-net/). It renders SVG without a browser or external tools. Install it with pip:

```bash
pip install aspose-svg-net
```

Save this `sample.svg` (400 × 300 pixels, no background) to follow along:

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="300" viewBox="0 0 400 300">
  <rect x="20" y="20" width="160" height="100" fill="#4A90E2" stroke="#1F3B63" stroke-width="4"/>
  <circle cx="290" cy="80" r="55" fill="#F5A623" stroke="#8B5A00" stroke-width="4"/>
  <line x1="20" y1="170" x2="380" y2="170" stroke="#333333" stroke-width="3"/>
  <text x="200" y="240" font-family="Arial" font-size="36" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2C3E50">Aspose.SVG</text>
</svg>
```

## Convert an SVG File to PNG in Python

Follow these steps to convert an SVG file to PNG:

1. Create an `ImageSaveOptions` object. PNG is its default format.
2. Set `page_setup.sizing` to `SizingType.FIT_CONTENT` so the PNG is cropped to the drawing.
3. Set the horizontal and vertical resolution.
4. Pass the SVG file path, the options, and the output path to `Converter.convert_svg()`.

The following code example converts `sample.svg` to a 400 × 300 PNG:

```python
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import ImageSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType
from aspose.svg.drawing import Resolution

options = ImageSaveOptions()  # PNG by default
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT
# 96 DPI keeps the SVG's own pixel size
options.horizontal_resolution = Resolution.from_dots_per_inch(96.0)
options.vertical_resolution = Resolution.from_dots_per_inch(96.0)

Converter.convert_svg("sample.svg", options, "sample.png")
```

Two defaults are worth knowing:

* **Page size:** without `FIT_CONTENT`, the drawing is placed on an A4 page.
* **Resolution:** the default is 300 DPI. With `FIT_CONTENT` but no resolution set, this 400 × 300 SVG becomes a 1250 × 938 PNG.

## Set the PNG Size

Because SVG units are treated as 1/96 inch, the PNG size equals the SVG size multiplied by `DPI / 96`. To produce a 2× image for high-density screens, use 192 DPI:

```python
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import ImageSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType
from aspose.svg.drawing import Resolution

options = ImageSaveOptions()
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT
# 192 DPI produces an 800 x 600 PNG from a 400 x 300 SVG
options.horizontal_resolution = Resolution.from_dots_per_inch(192.0)
options.vertical_resolution = Resolution.from_dots_per_inch(192.0)

Converter.convert_svg("sample.svg", options, "sample@2x.png")
```

`Resolution.from_dots_per_inch()` expects a float, so write `192.0`, not `192`.

## Convert an SVG from a URL to PNG

You can pass a URL instead of a file path. The library downloads the SVG and renders it:

```python
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import ImageSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType

options = ImageSaveOptions()
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT

Converter.convert_svg("https://www.w3.org/Icons/SVG/svg-logo-v.svg", options, "svg-logo.png")
```

If you want to inspect or edit the SVG before rendering, load it with `svg.SVGDocument(url)` first and pass the document to `convert_svg()`.

## Keep Transparency or Add a Background 

By default, the PNG is transparent wherever the SVG doesn't paint anything. That's usually what you want for icons. When the image will be placed on a dark page or in a viewer that shows transparency as black, set a solid background:

```python
import aspose.pydrawing as drawing
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import ImageSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType

options = ImageSaveOptions()
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT
options.background_color = drawing.Color.white

Converter.convert_svg("sample.svg", options, "sample-white.png")
```

## Batch Convert SVG to PNG

To convert an entire folder, reuse one options object in a loop. The example also catches errors, so one broken file doesn't stop the batch:

```python
import os
import glob
from aspose.svg.converters import Converter
from aspose.svg.saving import ImageSaveOptions
from aspose.svg.rendering import SizingType
from aspose.svg.drawing import Resolution

input_dir = "svg-files"
output_dir = "png-files"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

options = ImageSaveOptions()
options.page_setup.sizing = SizingType.FIT_CONTENT
options.horizontal_resolution = Resolution.from_dots_per_inch(96.0)
options.vertical_resolution = Resolution.from_dots_per_inch(96.0)

for svg_path in glob.glob(os.path.join(input_dir, "*.svg")):
    name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(svg_path))[0]
    png_path = os.path.join(output_dir, name + ".png")
    try:
        Converter.convert_svg(svg_path, options, png_path)
        print("Converted:", png_path)
    except Exception as error:
        print("Failed:", svg_path, error)
```

## SVG to PNG in Python: FAQs

**Q: Does the PNG keep the SVG's transparent background?**

A: Yes. Unpainted areas stay transparent unless you set `background_color`.

**Q: How do I get a PNG with the same pixel size as the SVG?**

A: Use `SizingType.FIT_CONTENT` and set both resolutions to 96 DPI.

**Q: Can I convert SVG markup stored in a string?**

A: Yes. Load it with `SVGDocument(svg_string, base_uri)`. The [SVG code to PNG](https://blog.aspose.com/svg/convert-svg-code-to-png-in-python/) article covers this case.

## Conclusion

You've converted SVG to PNG in Python from a file and from a URL, sized the PNG through its DPI, and set up a batch loop for a folder of files.
